title: CSV to Nested JSON Tree
input_format:
The first line contains an integer `n`, the number of data rows.
The second line is the CSV header `id,parentId,name`.
Each of the next `n` lines is one row `id,parentId,name` (no spaces).
output_format: Print the nested JSON array of root nodes on one line, in the compact format described above.
constraints: The forest has depth at most 500 (a root has depth 1)

examples.explanation: Nodes 1 and 5 are roots. Node 1 has children 2 and 3 (in row order), and node 3 has the child 4.
Node 7 appears before its parent 9, which is allowed. Under node 9 the children keep their CSV order: 7 first, then 4.

hints: First read every row into a map from id to its data, and a map from parentId to the list of child ids in row order. Do this before trying to link anything, because parents can come after their children.
The roots are the rows whose parentId is null. Everything else hangs below one of them.
Build the output string by walking the tree from the roots. Each node prints its header, then its children separated by commas, then the closing brackets.

import sys
sys.setrecursionlimit(10000)

data = sys.stdin.read().split()
n = int(data[0])
rows = [r.split(',') for r in data[2:2 + n]]

def node(i, nm):
    kids = [node(int(r[0]), r[2]) for r in rows if r[1] == str(i)]
    return '{"id":' + str(i) + ',"name":"' + nm + '","children":[' + ','.join(kids) + ']}'

print('[' + ','.join(node(int(r[0]), r[2]) for r in rows if r[1] == 'null') + ']')
